// Part: room: powder room (interior furnisher + lamplighter). Inner air x63..68, y4..9, z54..60.
// Door from the east corridor at z53 (x65..66). Focal piece: the washstand on the south wall (z60), basin and mirror
// facing the door. Chair (stairs) at z59 facing it, a 3x3 rug in the middle, a barrel with a pot in the north-east
// corner, a hanging lantern over the rug and a standing lantern on the floor at the south-west of the rug. The west doorway (x62, z56..57) and the south windows (x65..66, z61) stay clear.
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  const legend = {
    B: "barrel",
    F: "flower_pot",
    W: "white_carpet",
    S: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "north", half: "bottom" }],
    K: "dark_oak_planks",
    C: "water_cauldron",
    G: "glass_pane",
    I: "iron_bars",
    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
    T: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
  };
  // rows run along +x (x63..68), successive rows along +z (z54..60); one layer per y (y4..y9)
  const EMPTY = "......";
  layers(g, [63, 4, 54], legend, [
    // y4 floor: barrel NE corner, rug x64..66 z56..58, chair z59, washstand cabinet x63..64 z60
    [".....B", EMPTY, ".WWW..", ".WWW..", ".TWW..", ".S....", "KK...."],
    // y5: pot on the barrel, water basin and a pot on the washstand
    [".....F", EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, "CF...."],
    // y6..7: mirror panes on the wall behind the basin
    [EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, "GG...."],
    [EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, "GG...."],
    // y8: iron bar cornice over the mirror
    [EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, "II...."],
    // y9: hanging lantern over the rug (the upper floor at y10 is the hanging block)
    [EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY, "..L...", EMPTY, EMPTY, EMPTY],
  ]);
}

input.summary:
Room-10 (powder room) writes its 23 furnishings, but every cell in its box is air that the shell owns (shell.mjs box() fills x27..68, y3..17, z43..60 with air), so runParts refuses all 23 and the part places 0 blocks.
Off-palette: none. Every block in the legend is in palette.json and passes `mcd blocks --check`.
REFUSED is not fixed. Nothing inside room-10 can be written without editing shell.mjs or bypassing the lock, and neither is allowed here. parts/room-10.mjs is unchanged.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owned the refused cells: reading runParts' lock code in build.mjs and shell.mjs box() to see that the shell's air fill is what locks the room.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and roughly 100 lines of library source read
waste.tool: runParts should name the owning part and the rule for each refused cell (e.g. 'owned by shell: air fill x27..68 y3..17 z43..60'), and mcd plan should list which cells of a room box a later part can still write.

waste.what: Working out the 23 refused cells cell by cell from the six layers, because parts-report.json keeps only the first 8 refusals.
waste.cost: one manual pass over six layers of the legend; the report gives 8 of 23
waste.tool: parts-report.json should carry the full refused list, or a per-room summary of refused cells by block.

waste.what: Checking palette compliance by hand. The OFF-PALETTE check counts only successful writes, so a fully refused part reports nothing.
waste.cost: one mcd blocks --check call plus a manual compare with palette.json
waste.tool: runParts should run the palette check on attempted writes as well as successful ones, or mcd palette should accept a layers() legend.

companions.task: Fit the powder room's washstand cabinet, mirror frame and barrel once the shell leaves the room's air open to furnishing; the joinery work has no place to go while the air is locked.

left: REFUSED 23 writes remain. Every cell in the powder room box (x63..68, y4..9, z54..60) is air that shell.mjs box() filled and runParts locks, so no write inside the room can succeed. The fix belongs upstream: either shell.mjs leaves room air unfilled, or runParts treats air inside rooms.json boxes as writable for room parts. That needs an owner decision because it changes the lock contract.
make.sh still produces build.nbt, but this room has 0 blocks in it (no furniture, rug, lanterns, or mirror panes).
Off-palette is clear for the writes as written, but the palette check ran on zero placed writes, so it has not been exercised. Re-check after the lock is resolved.
The other room parts (room-1 to room-37 apart from this one) place 0 blocks now. The same lock will refuse their furnishing once they are written, so the upstream fix affects all rooms.

Room-10 (powder room) writes its 23 furnishings, but every cell in its box is air that the shell owns (shell.mjs box() fills x27..68, y3..17, z43..60 with air), so runParts refuses all 23 and the part places 0 blocks.
Off-palette: none. Every block in the legend is in palette.json and passes `mcd blocks --check`.
REFUSED is not fixed. Nothing inside room-10 can be written without editing shell.mjs or bypassing the lock, and neither is allowed here. parts/room-10.mjs is unchanged.
